absent: Underlying attribute carrying allocation, mapping, unmapping and coherent user mapping implementations behind the wrappers.
Worker behavior for single and scatter gather synchronization and for address need probing.
Skip synchronization predicate and debug audit selection beyond the need expression.
Paged allocation and release, debug mapping hook and mapping error indicator value.
Coherent mask, streaming mask, segment parameter storage and device parameter allocation lifecycle.
Numeric values for 64K size, all ones boundary, 32 bit mask helpers and minimum DMA alignment.
Second parameter and full contract of the result carrying completion callback whose declaration is truncated.
Channel switching enablement condition and switching transfer semantics.
RAID offload effect on unmap accounting beyond counter width.
Peripheral blob format, router release semantics and slave table matching rules.
Cache line group delimiter behavior and write combining memory ordering guarantees.
Device name string lifetime and channel sysfs presentation details.

findings.text: Noncoherent allocation provides paged allocation exposed as a kernel address with null indicating failure, and release accepts such an address for paged release.

Single buffer mapping is restricted to memory that cannot be remapped and is covered by mapping audit, with valid requests served through paged mapping using page and offset; single unmapping is served through paged unmapping.
Ranged synchronization covers a subrange identified by base device address plus offset with the given length, in processor and device orientations.
Table based unmapping and synchronization operate on the stored scatter list using the recorded original entry count in either transfer orientation.
Attribute less mapping, unmapping, paged transfer, table retrieval and coherent user mapping forms are provided as aliases that supply zero attributes to the attribute carrying forms.

Coherent allocation carries a no warning attribute exactly when the allocation request asks to suppress warnings, and coherent release plus managed coherent allocation follow the same attribute discipline with managed allocation preserving the warning hint.
Write combining memory is allocated with write combining always requested while preserving any warning suppression hint, and release plus user mapping of such memory always request write combining.
Channel naming exposes the device name associated with the channel device object.

Channel selection is expressed as a predicate over channel and opaque selector, completion notification is expressed through plain and result carrying callbacks, and transfer outcome distinguishes success from read failure, write failure and abort with an accompanying residual length.

In the routed build the IOVA path is unavailable: use and allocation probes report negative, release and destroy have no observable effect, synchronization and linking report unsupported operation, and unlinking has no observable effect.

Synchronization need is build dependent. One build always reports no need with all single, scatter gather and probe operations having no effect and negative answers. The other build reports need whenever skipping is not permitted and always under mapping audit, with synchronization and address probing effective only under need and otherwise inert.

Effective DMA mask defaults to 32 bit coverage when no device mask storage holds a value. Coherent mask update requires prior success of the streaming mask update. Coerced mask setup requires aliasing of streaming mask storage to coherent storage.

Segment constraints provide a 64K maximum size fallback, an all ones boundary fallback and a zero minimal alignment fallback when device parameters or fields are absent. Updates without allocated parameters are ignored with a one time warning, otherwise the stored constraint is replaced.
Segment boundary expressed in pages corresponds to the applicable boundary shifted by page order plus one, with a 32 bit all ones basis when no device is given.

Unmap bookkeeping has a storing build where owner objects hold a device address and a 32 bit length with direct access, and a non storing build where address and length reads yield zero and writes have no effect while still checking the owner pointer.

Descriptor neighbor linkage is build dependent. Without switching support neighbor queries yield null and clearing has no effect while linkage attempts fault. With support linkage establishes mutual forward and backward references, clearing nulls the selected side, and queries return the stored neighbor.

Unmap attachment either records the supplied state with reference bookkeeping or has no effect depending on build. Descriptor release is inert without recorded state, otherwise it drops the state and clears the link. The stub provider always yields null with inert release.

A channel object combines parent device linkage with optional slave linkage, issued and completed progress cookies, exclusion state, numeric identity with device object and name for presentation, list linkage into device channels, per processor accounting, client and table counts, optional router linkage with opaque route data, and opaque private context, plus a debug only client name.

A transfer descriptor combines an assignment cookie with control flags sized to pack alongside it, a persistent device visible address, owning channel linkage, submission and release operations, plain and result carrying completion handlers sharing one parameter, optional unmap linkage, metadata mode with handler table, and optional forward backward linkage with exclusion state for switching builds.

Slave endpoint programming combines transfer orientation, source and destination addresses, per side address widths, per side burst caps, per side port window extents, a device managed flow control selector, and an opaque peripheral blob given by pointer plus length.

Slave capability reporting combines acceptable width masks per side, allowed orientations, minimum and maximum burst lengths with a scatter gather burst cap, pause resume and terminate command availability, residue precision selector, and descriptor reuse support.

Interleaved programming combines start addresses per side, orientation, per side increment and scatter gather selectors, frame count with frame extent, and a trailing array of chunks each giving transfer extent with overall and per side gaps. A vector combines a device address with a length.

Unmap accounting combines a mapped entry count whose width grows under RAID offload, one way and bidirectional subcounts, mapping device linkage, a reference count with total length, and a trailing array of device addresses.
Descriptor metadata handling combines attachment of external memory, pointer retrieval reporting payload and capacity extents, and payload length update.
Transfer progress combines the latest completed cookie with the latest issued cookie, remaining length, and bytes currently in flight.
Static channel routing combines a selection predicate with table length and table pointer, where each entry pairs device and slave names with an opaque selector.

Routing support pairs a device with a release handler for opaque route data. Channel device objects link back to the channel with numeric identity and a DMA device marker. Per processor counters track completed copies and moved bytes.
Channel configuration and transfer preparation share one spin lock because preparation can originate in completion processing where sleeping is forbidden.
Descriptor linkage exclusion is inert without switching support and provides mutual exclusion around neighbor updates with support.

Transfer observation distinguishes completion, ongoing progress, held pause, failure, and completion out of order, where completion and failure are terminal and the others permit further progress or control.

Completion outcome distinguishes success from source failure, destination failure and abort, always with residual length. Residue accuracy is limited to descriptor, segment or burst precision as advertised by the channel.
Submission checking treats negative cookies as error codes passed through unchanged and all other cookies as success, with one as the smallest valid cookie.
Supplying remappable virtual memory for single mapping triggers a one time device warning and yields the mapping error indicator rather than a usable address.
Updating segment limits or alignment without allocated device parameters triggers a one time warning and preserves existing stored values.
Requesting descriptor linkage without switching support faults instead of establishing any link.
Cookies use a signed 32 bit representation with one as the minimum valid value and negative values reserved for errors.
Status codes map DMA_COMPLETE to first, DMA_IN_PROGRESS to second, DMA_PAUSED to third, DMA_ERROR to fourth and DMA_OUT_OF_ORDER to last.
Capabilities begin with DMA_MEMCPY for copy, DMA_XOR for parity, DMA_PQ for dual parity, DMA_XOR_VAL and DMA_PQ_VAL for verification, DMA_MEMSET for fill and DMA_MEMSET_SG for scattered fill.

Remaining capabilities provide DMA_INTERRUPT for signaling, DMA_PRIVATE with DMA_ASYNC_TX for internal use, DMA_SLAVE with DMA_CYCLIC and DMA_INTERLEAVE for peripheral patterns, DMA_COMPLETION_NO_ORDER for relaxed ordering, DMA_REPEAT with DMA_LOAD_EOT for repetition control, closed by DMA_TX_TYPE_END as terminator.
Orientation offers DMA_MEM_TO_MEM for internal moves, DMA_MEM_TO_DEV for transmit, DMA_DEV_TO_MEM for receive, DMA_DEV_TO_DEV for peer moves, and DMA_TRANS_NONE for idle.
Low control bits place DMA_PREP_INTERRUPT at bit zero, DMA_CTRL_ACK at bit one, DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P at bit two with DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q at bit three, and DMA_PREP_CONTINUE at bit four.
High control bits place DMA_PREP_FENCE at bit five, DMA_CTRL_REUSE at bit six, DMA_PREP_CMD at bit seven, DMA_PREP_REPEAT at bit eight and DMA_PREP_LOAD_EOT at bit nine.
Check selectors define SUM_CHECK_P as zero with SUM_CHECK_Q as one, and result masks define SUM_CHECK_P_RESULT with SUM_CHECK_Q_RESULT at matching bit positions.
Capability masks are bitmaps sized by the transaction terminator. Metadata modes define DESC_METADATA_NONE as zero, DESC_METADATA_CLIENT at the first bit and DESC_METADATA_ENGINE at the second bit.
Residue precision defines DMA_RESIDUE_GRANULARITY_DESCRIPTOR as zero for coarsest, DMA_RESIDUE_GRANULARITY_SEGMENT as one, and DMA_RESIDUE_GRANULARITY_BURST as two for finest.

Alignment codes map DMAENGINE_ALIGN_1_BYTE to zero, DMAENGINE_ALIGN_2_BYTES to one, DMAENGINE_ALIGN_4_BYTES to two, DMAENGINE_ALIGN_8_BYTES to three, DMAENGINE_ALIGN_16_BYTES to four, DMAENGINE_ALIGN_32_BYTES to five, DMAENGINE_ALIGN_64_BYTES to six, DMAENGINE_ALIGN_128_BYTES to seven, and DMAENGINE_ALIGN_256_BYTES to eight.

Bus widths start with DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_UNDEFINED as zero, DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_1_BYTE as one, DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_2_BYTES as two, DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_3_BYTES as three, DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_4_BYTES as four, and DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_8_BYTES as eight.

Wide bus widths continue with DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_16_BYTES as sixteen, DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_32_BYTES as thirty two, DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_64_BYTES as sixty four, and DMA_SLAVE_BUSWIDTH_128_BYTES as one hundred twenty eight.
From device grouping requests minimum DMA alignment in one build and no extra alignment in the other, with begin and end markers wrapping cache line group delimiters.
The DMA engine header provides a single inclusion guard.
